items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: I did a lot of work with this fado singer Ana Moura, and it was just after my mother died I wrote this song

ctx.x: Well again I feel it’s just the music is there and you know whether it’s like I’m just capturing it and not getting in the way of it, which is kind of what happened in that situation where this song I wrote, the song “Saint Michel” which is based on that you know, 70 or so people being killed. And had it not been a beautiful day, if it had been raining I would have been on that train because it was so nice I’m going to walk. It’s going to take me an hour but I’m going to be outside, Paris the greatest city for…

but I wrote that song because it just was like, it just came out, I didn’t think actually, it really just came out. And that’s happened a number of times in my life where it’s just like I feel these things happen. In fact my mother died really tragically very quickly, and she used to talk about guardian angels. And so I wrote a song called “Guardian Angels” that came out on one of my records and then so she used to talk about this that my brother who died was like watching over me. So then I remember I did a lot…

I’ve often wondered, song titles can be obvious or is it possible to write a tune and say I don’t know what to call this. And the fact that you hadn’t titled it left that opening for him perhaps, or maybe he would have gone there anyway but it’s a great story.
